title: Rigveda 9.42: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.42: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.42 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 682v-683r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.42.1-4 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 32); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 682v
translation.original_text:
1ja̱naya̍n roca̱nā di̱vo ja̱naya̍nn a̱psu sūrya̍m | vasā̍no̱ gā a̱po hari̍ḥ ||
2e̱ṣa pra̱tnena̱ manma̍nā de̱vo de̱vebhya̱s pari̍ | dhāra̍yā pavate su̱taḥ ||
3vā̱vṛ̱dhā̱nāya̱ tūrva̍ye̱ pava̍nte̱ vāja̍sātaye | somā̍ḥ sa̱hasra̍pājasaḥ ||
4du̱hā̱naḥ pra̱tnam it paya̍ḥ pa̱vitre̱ pari̍ ṣicyate | kranda̍n de̱vām̐ a̍jījanat ||
translation.text:
1ENGENDERING the Sun in floods, engendering heaven's lights, green-hued, Robed in the waters and the milk,
2According to primeval plan this Soma, with his stream, effused Flows purely on, a God for Gods.
3For him victorious, waxen great, the juices with a thousand powers Are purified for winning spoil.
4Shedding the ancient fluid he is poured into the cleansing sieve: He, thundering, hath produced the Gods.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 682v (numbered 104v by the scribe) (OPenn image 683, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.41.1 ‹ayāsaḥ akramuḥ ghnantaḥ kṛṣṇām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 683r (numbered 105r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.42.5 ‹abhi viśvāni vāryā abhi›. Verses 9.42.1-4 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1janayan | rocanā | divaḥ | janayan | ap-su | sūryam | vasānaḥ | gāḥ | apaḥ | hariḥ
2eṣaḥ | pratnena | manmanā | devaḥ | devebhyaḥ | pari | dhārayā | pavate | sutaḥ
3vavṛdhānāya | tūrvaye | pavante | vāja-sātaye | somāḥ | sahasra-pājasaḥ
4duhānaḥ | pratnam | it | payaḥ | pavitre | pari | sicyate | krandan | devān | ajījanat

translation.original_ref: RV 9.42.5-6 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 32); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 683r
translation.original_text:
5a̱bhi viśvā̍ni̱ vāryā̱bhi de̱vām̐ ṛ̍tā̱vṛdha̍ḥ | soma̍ḥ punā̱no a̍rṣati ||
6goma̍n naḥ soma vī̱rava̱d aśvā̍va̱d vāja̍vat su̱taḥ | pava̍sva bṛha̱tīr iṣa̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
5Soma, while purifying, sends hither all things to be desired, He sends the Gods who strengthen Law.
6Soma, effused, pour on us wealth in kine, in heroes, steeds, and spoil, Send us abundant store of food.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 683r (numbered 105r by the scribe) (OPenn image 683, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.42.5 ‹abhi viśvāni vāryā abhi›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 684v (numbered 1v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.44.1 ‹pra naḥ indo iti›. Verses 9.42.5-6 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
5abhi | viśvāni | vāryā | abhi | devān | ṛta-vṛdhaḥ | somaḥ | punānaḥ | arṣati
6go-mat | naḥ | soma | vīra-vat | aśva-vat | vāja-vat | sutaḥ | pavasva | bṛhatīḥ | iṣaḥ
